Ticket Id: 24560

05/07/2014

Dr B White
Neurosurgeon
City Hospital
Newtown

Dear Dr White,
RE: Mr George Poulos, aged 45 years

I am writing to refer this patient who is demonstrating signs and symptoms presumptive of discogenic low              Commented [ESL1]: ,
back pain associated with radiculopathy for further investigations and management.                                    Commented [ESL2]: ,


The patient is a heavy smoker and his alcohol consumption is excessive. Please note, he is allergic to
pethidine, penicillin, unspecified radiographic contrast agent and possibly iodine.

Initially, when the patient presented to me on 21/06/2014, he was complaining of a tow- day history of                Commented [ESL3]: two-day
sudden severe middle lower back pain that was described as a click sensation for which he took two
Panadeine Forte. On examination, there was loss of lumbar lordosis, painful flexion of fingertips to patella,
and limited extension due to pain. However, his lateral flexion, rotation, and sensation were normal.
Therefore, paracetamol was instituted and rest was advised. One week later, his condition has further                 Commented [ESL4]: had
deteriorated.

Today, the patient pain has worsened along with being almost immobile and tingling sensation in his right             Commented [ESL5]: experiencing a
calf. His examination showed no lumber flexion, restriction of most movements because of pain, decreased
SLR (left 70 and right 50), loss of right ankle reflexes, and loss of light touch sensation over the lateral distal
calf and the planter aspect of foot.                                                                                  Commented [ESL6]: the


I believe the patient needs MRI and to provide advice regarding the likelihood of surgery.                            Commented [ESL7]: an


Thank you for your expert care and kindly feel free to contact me if any more information is required.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
